effects.log: The herald, who has not been offered tea in four hundred years, sits down and drinks three cups. The honours go unread.

events.text: {npc} has a tradition: every hundred years, a small gift, never expensive, always odd. This century's gift is a pebble from the Sea of Clouds that, when held to the ear, hums the first song you ever danced to. {He} gives it to you in the kitchen without ceremony.

choices.text: Hold it to your ear and listen

mem.note: gave me the pebble that hums our first dance

effects.log: The song is faint and a little out of tune. You listen to the whole of it, standing in the kitchen, and the tea boils over.

choices.text: Give a gift in return, a worse one

mem.note: received a clumsy bundle of old letters

effects.log: Your gift is a poorly tied bundle of old letters. {npc} reads them one at a time over a week and weeps at three.

events.text: On the thousand-and-first year {npc} sits you down and says they have been thinking about what the thousand years were for. {He} does not say it was the road, or the breakthroughs, or the House. {He} says: "The tea." You nod, because you have known it for centuries.

choices.text: Make a fresh pot and sit through the afternoon

mem.note: knew the thousand years were for the tea

effects.log: You make the tea, and the afternoon is a long, warm, unremarkable thing. It is the best afternoon of your thousand years.

choices.text: Begin planning the second thousand

mem.note: planned the next thousand years over tea

effects.log: The second thousand begins with a list. {npc} reads it and adds, at the bottom, in careful brush: more tea.

events.text: The pebble stops humming one day, as stones do. {npc} is quietly devastated and tries to hide it. You find them on the terrace holding the stone in two hands. "I have lost the song," {he} says. "I knew it would end. I did not think I would miss it so."

choices.text: Hum the song yourself

mem.note: hummed our song when the stone went quiet

effects.log: You hum it, badly. {npc} laughs, and then hums along, and the two of you carry the tune, off-key, for the rest of the evening.

choices.text: Set the stone in a small shrine in the garden

mem.note: built a shrine for the silent stone

effects.log: The stone sits under a small roof in the garden. The song is gone, but you visit, sometimes, and sit.

events.text: {npc} has been summoned by an examiner of the Jade Court's Rolls, who hints that a seat as an Assessor of Merit might be on offer. {He} wants it, badly, and does not say so. At dinner {he} asks, with studied lightness, whether you would mind a long posting at the Court.
events.arc: A Post at the Jade Court

choices.text: Tell {him} to take it, and mean it

mem.note: told me to take the Court post

effects.log: "Take it," you say. {npc} stares, then hugs you hard, and sits up half the night drafting a petition.

choices.text: Ask what it would cost the household

mem.note: asked what my post would cost you

effects.log: You ask in good faith. {npc} hears the price in the question, and goes quiet. The seat is not decided that night.

choices.text: Say you would rather they stayed

mem.note: asked me to turn down the Court post

effects.log: {npc} bows {his} head. "Then I will stay," {he} says, and you both know it is not the same as agreeing.

events.text: The Court's examination for the post is a fortnight of riddles, memory-tests, and flattery. {npc} is brilliant, and worried. On the last night, {he} shows you a rival's name on the list: a Lord of the Nine Peaks who has bought half the examiners.
events.arc: A Post at the Jade Court

choices.text: Help {him} study the Lord's weaknesses

mem.note: helped me beat a bought rival

effects.log: You research the Lord and find those ledgers slipshod. {npc} uses it with delicacy and the Lord withdraws.

choices.text: Tell {him} to win it honestly or not at all

mem.note: told me to win honestly

effects.log: {npc} stands very straight. {He} takes the exam honestly, and comes second, and is offered a lesser seat in the end.

events.text: The result arrives by crane: {npc} is an Assessor of Merit, on the Court's twelfth terrace. The household celebrates. Then {npc} reads the posting: forty years at the Court, rarely home. {He} looks at you across the table, and does not ask you to decide.
events.arc: A Post at the Jade Court

choices.text: Move to the Court with {him}

mem.note: brought you to the Court with me

effects.log: You move your life to the twelfth terrace. It is smaller, colder, and full of politics. {npc} is happier than you have ever seen.

choices.text: Stay home and write every season

mem.note: wrote to me every season of my posting

effects.log: You stay. The letters go back and forth in a quiet stream, and the household settles into an odd and affectionate rhythm.

events.text: The seat you urged them to refuse, and they did not, goes badly. {npc} spends a decade sullen and underused in a cheaper office of the Court, and one night says it aloud: "I should have fought for the better seat. Or I should have never gone at all."
events.arc: A Post at the Jade Court

choices.text: Own that you were part of it

mem.note: owned up to the part you played in my bad post

effects.log: You say you were. {npc} nods slowly. It does not fix it, but it lets the room breathe again.

choices.text: Offer to petition the Court for a better seat

mem.note: petitioned for a better seat for me

effects.log: The petition is a long, dull campaign. Within the decade, {npc} is promoted. The thanks are quiet, and enormous.

events.text: {npc} spreads a roll of plans across the table: a pavilion on a small unclaimed isle, three terraces, a library, a school. {He} has been drawing it for a century. "I want to found it," {he} says. "I will need an endowment, a charter, and your name on the petition."

choices.text: Put your name on the petition

mem.note: signed my pavilion petition

effects.log: You sign. The petition, with two names, goes to the Court on the next crane. {npc} frames the first draft.

choices.text: Fund it quietly without a name

mem.note: secretly funded my pavilion

effects.log: You fund the endowment from your own stones and tell no one. {npc} learns eventually, and is neither pleased nor displeased, and silent for a day.

choices.text: Suggest they build it smaller

mem.note: told me to dream smaller

effects.log: You suggest a pavilion half the size. {npc} thinks about it for a week, resentful, and half agrees.

events.text: The Court's Surveyor visits the isle and finds a boundary dispute: the Clan of the Nine Peaks claims the eastern cliff. {npc} will have to give up a terrace or take the matter before the Court. {He} is fierce, tired, and looking at you with the face of a person who wants advice.

choices.text: Advise a compromise: give up the terrace

mem.note: gave up a terrace on your advice

effects.log: You advise the terrace go. {npc} grumbles, then sends the Nine Peaks a gift. The pavilion is built, smaller, and sound.

choices.text: Advise fighting the claim before the Court

mem.note: fought the Nine Peaks for the cliff with you

effects.log: You advise the fight. The Court hears the case for a year. {npc} wins the cliff, and spends the next century defending it.

events.text: The pavilion opens on a cold spring morning with a ribbon of cloud-silk and a bell that rings all of one note. A hundred guests come. {npc}, in a plain robe, makes a speech that lasts four sentences, and the last one is your name.

choices.text: Rise and bow to the guests

mem.note: named you at the opening of my pavilion

effects.log: You rise. The guests applaud. {npc}, seeing it, has to stop and wipe their eyes.

choices.text: Stay seated and let {him} have the day

mem.note: let me have my pavilion day

effects.log: You stay seated. {npc} looks for you in the crowd and finds you, and the speech is better for it.

events.text: A century into the pavilion's life, a School of the Nine Peaks is founded across the water, with an eye to rivalry. {npc} frets. Their pupils are fewer, the Nine Peaks' endowment richer, and the long fight over the cliff has not been forgotten by the Clan.

choices.text: Propose a joint competition between the schools

mem.note: proposed a joint contest for our school

effects.log: The competition is a friendly, grandiose thing. Both schools sing. {npc}'s pupils win the poetry; the Nine Peaks the swords. Honour is even.

choices.text: Offer the Nine Peaks a seat on the pavilion's board

mem.note: made the Nine Peaks a seat on our board

effects.log: The offer stuns the Clan. It is accepted. The cliff is, in time, a shared garden.

events.text: The Celestial Ministries are sending an expedition into a Sky Rift, a tear in the clouds that exhales strange light. They need a leader who knows the old routes. {npc} has been proposed. {He} wants it more than {he} will admit, and is watching your face for the verdict.

choices.text: Tell {him} to lead it

mem.note: told me to lead the Rift expedition

effects.log: "You will be brilliant," you say. {npc} breathes out like a sword drawn, and begins to plan.

choices.text: Offer to go with the expedition

mem.note: came with me into the Rift

effects.log: You volunteer to go. {npc} hesitates, then accepts, glad and afraid. The Ministries enrol you as a second.

choices.text: Warn that the Rifts have taken leaders before

mem.note: warned me off the Rift

effects.log: You warn, honestly, and {npc} listens. The warning is true. The look on {his} face says it was not the thing to say.

events.text: The expedition goes through the Rift and does not come back on schedule. A season passes. At the Ministries' station you wait with the other families, and a clerk reads the list of the returning. {npc}'s name is not on it. The clerk says there is a signal, faint, from the far side.

choices.text: Wait at the station and answer the signal

mem.note: answered my signal from the Rift

effects.log: You answer the signal with a pulse of qi, the code you and {npc} agreed. A faint reply, then a stronger.

choices.text: Request permission to enter the Rift and bring them back

mem.note: came into the Rift to find me

effects.log: The Ministries refuse for a month and grant it on the thirtieth day. You step into the light.

events.text: The expedition returns: three of eleven lost, eight carrying a ghostly map of the Rift's far side. {npc} steps off the cloud-barge limping and silent. The Ministries wish to honour {him}. {npc} wishes to sit down. They find you in the crowd and sit, gratefully, on your shoulder.

choices.text: Take {him} home before the speeches

mem.note: took me home before the Rift speeches

effects.log: You carry {npc} home and put them to bed. The Ministries' speeches go on without a hero. The hero sleeps for three days.

choices.text: Stand beside {him} at the honouring

mem.note: stood beside me at the Rift honouring

effects.log: You stand through the whole honouring, hand on their elbow. {npc} stays upright because you do.

events.text: The Rift, when {npc} left it, was alive with strange breath. Now they cannot stop talking about its far side, and the Ministries have asked for a second expedition. {He} does not ask your leave this time. {He} tells you, and waits for what you will say.

choices.text: Say go, and I will hold the household

mem.note: held the house for my second Rift journey

effects.log: "I will hold it," you say. {npc} kisses you and begins packing. You know the expedition will outlast the next two decades.

choices.text: Say I am coming this time

mem.note: came on my second Rift journey

effects.log: You are coming. The Ministries, short of staff, agree. {npc} smiles like a person given a sword they did not ask for.

events.text: {npc} is climbing faster than you. A sleepless year, a lucky dream, a master's blessing: whatever the cause, {his} realm is a step above yours now, and the household's visitors address {him} first. You are happy for {him}. You are also, to your private embarrassment, not entirely happy.
events.arc: The Spouse Who Rose Past You

choices.text: Admit the feeling to {him}

mem.note: admitted they envied my rise

effects.log: You admit it, gruffly, over tea. {npc} nods. "I felt it for you, once," {he} says. "It passes. It leaves a mark."

choices.text: Throw yourself into your own cultivation

mem.note: trained in silence while I rose

effects.log: You spend a decade in training. You do not catch up, but you stop being tired of the gap.

choices.text: Pretend not to mind

mem.note: pretended not to mind my rise

effects.log: You pretend not to mind. {npc} sees through it in a week and says nothing. The silence has a cost.

events.text: At a banquet the Court's elder introduces {npc} as "the one who will take the House" and you as "the companion." The word lands like a pebble on a bell. {npc} stands and corrects the elder, gently, with a precise and public list of your accomplishments.
events.arc: The Spouse Who Rose Past You

choices.text: Thank {him} in front of the elder

mem.note: corrected the elder on my behalf

effects.log: You thank {npc} with a bow that the elder notices. The elder goes on carefully, and the banquet drifts onward.

choices.text: Say later that you wanted to speak for yourself

mem.note: apologised for speaking over you

effects.log: "I know," says {npc}, quiet. "I did it too fast. I'm sorry." The apology costs {him} something, and you take it.

events.text: A decade on, you cross a threshold of your own, not a realm but a clarity, a quiet understanding that does not need to be above or below. {npc} feels it from across the grotto and looks up, hearing something new in the air. "There you are," {he} says, as if you had been lost.
events.arc: The Spouse Who Rose Past You

choices.text: Sit with {him} and share what you saw

mem.note: taught me what they found while I rose

effects.log: You share it slowly. {npc} listens like a student. For the first time in a hundred years you are, for an hour, teaching.

choices.text: Say nothing and enjoy the quiet

mem.note: found their own clarity beside my rise

effects.log: You enjoy it. {npc} lets it be. The grotto is very warm, and the gap between you is no longer a gap.

events.text: {npc} goes beyond the next stair in a year, and the gap grows wider. They invite you to follow, and you cannot, not yet. At the threshold of the Court's Upper Gate {he} stops. "I will wait," {he} says, in the old words. "I do not know how long. Take the time you need."
events.arc: The Spouse Who Rose Past You

choices.text: Thank {him} and promise to follow

mem.note: went ahead and waited for me

effects.log: "I will follow," you say. {npc} nods. The Gate opens. You watch {him} go through, and the long wait begins.

choices.text: Tell {him} not to wait, and mean it kindly

mem.note: stayed at my speed instead of going ahead

effects.log: "Do not wait," you say. {npc} looks stricken, then understanding. "Then I will stay," {he} says, "and we will go together, at your speed."

events.text: The old Keeper of the Lotus Ledger is stepping down, and the seat is open. It is the quietest, most powerful post in the Jade Court: whoever holds the Ledger knows every name on the Rolls. {npc} wants it. {He} also knows what holding it does to a marriage.
events.arc: The Keeper of the Lotus Ledger

choices.text: Tell {him} you trust {him} with the Ledger

mem.note: trusted me with the Lotus Ledger

effects.log: "Then I will take it," says {npc}. The petition goes up, and you spend a season rehearsing answers to the Court's questions.

choices.text: Ask {him} to promise never to read your name

mem.note: asked me not to read your name

effects.log: {npc} gives the promise, solemn and absurd. You hold them both to it.

choices.text: Ask {him} to leave the Ledger to others

mem.note: asked me to leave the Ledger alone

effects.log: {npc} thinks it through, and does not answer for a week. When they do, they are silent about the post altogether.

events.text: The petition is accepted. {npc} takes the Keeper's brush, and in the first month finds a startling thing: the Ledger lists a number of couples married by error, couples who do not know. The clerks have been sitting on the corrections for centuries. {He} is appalled.
events.arc: The Keeper of the Lotus Ledger

choices.text: Help {him} write the corrections

mem.note: wrote to the mismatched couples with me

effects.log: You spend the winter drafting letters to eleven couples. Seven reply, and four write back with joy.

choices.text: Advise {him} to leave the old errors alone

mem.note: advised me to leave the old errors

effects.log: You advise leaving them. {npc} agrees reluctantly and keeps a private list of the unsettled, to revisit.

events.text: A decade into the Keeper's tenure, a visitor arrives from the Ministries with a request: a certain name is to be struck from the Rolls, quietly, for reasons of state. {npc} is alone in the Keeper's hall when it arrives, and sends you a note, urgent: "Come. I need you to tell me if I am being a fool."
events.arc: The Keeper of the Lotus Ledger

choices.text: Come and read the request together

mem.note: asked you if I was being a fool, and refused

effects.log: You read it. The reason is flimsy. {npc} refuses with a letter of cold courtesy, and the Ministries back down within the month.

choices.text: Tell {him} to comply and keep the peace

mem.note: struck a name on your advice

effects.log: You advise caution. {npc} strikes the name. A year later the person turns up alive and unharmed, and {npc} says nothing, and you say nothing, and both of you know.

events.text: {npc} has held the Ledger for a century, and looks it. The records have eaten sleep and appetite. One evening you find {him} asleep over the open book, brush still in hand. A single drop of ink has fallen on a page and spread into the shape of a plum blossom.
events.arc: The Keeper of the Lotus Ledger

choices.text: Wake {him} gently and bring tea

mem.note: woke me over the Ledger with tea

effects.log: You wake {him} with tea. {npc} looks at the ink blossom, and smiles. "I think I shall leave it," {he} says.

choices.text: Close the book and carry {him} to bed

mem.note: carried me from the Ledger to bed

effects.log: You carry {npc} to bed, and close the Ledger. The ink dries in the shape of a plum blossom, and stays on the page for ten thousand years.

events.text: The Celestial Ministries ask {npc} to serve as envoy to the Demon Realm: a dangerous posting, a diplomatic tightrope, and, if it works, a peace of a century. {He} has not said yes. {He} has told you, and is waiting at the window with the cloud-light on {his} face.
events.arc: An Envoy to the Demon Realm

choices.text: Tell {him} the Realm will respect them

mem.note: encouraged me to take the Realm posting

effects.log: You tell {him} the truth as you see it: that {he} is the right voice. {npc} nods, slow, and sends a reply to the Ministries.

choices.text: Ask what the Ministries will give for the risk

mem.note: asked the Ministries for a fair price

effects.log: You ask. The price is steep and the offer thin. {npc} turns it into a better offer in a week, and thanks you.

choices.text: Say you fear for {his} life

mem.note: feared for my life, honestly

effects.log: You say so. {npc} takes your hand and says it is a good fear, an honest fear, and will go anyway.

events.text: In the Demon Realm the envoy is received with silk and spears. {npc} writes home in a cipher that sounds nearly cheerful: the Demon Sovereign is a poor negotiator and a lovely host. A year of letters. Then the letters change in tone.
events.arc: An Envoy to the Demon Realm

choices.text: Write back in the old cipher and ask what has changed

mem.note: drafted peace terms with me by crane

effects.log: The reply comes slowly: a pressure, a faction, a threat. You help {npc} rewrite the terms by crane-post, a draft each season.

choices.text: Travel to the Realm and stand beside {him}

mem.note: crossed the border to stand with me

effects.log: You cross the border. The Realm's guards are stony and polite. {npc} sees you at the gate and puts a hand over their mouth.

events.text: The treaty is signed in a hall of black glass. {npc} puts the Ministries' seal beside the Sovereign's. In the corridor after, {he} drops the diplomat's face entirely and laughs, shakily. "We did it," {he} says. "Do you realise? We did the thing nobody could do."
events.arc: An Envoy to the Demon Realm

choices.text: Embrace {him} in the black corridor

mem.note: embraced me after the Realm treaty

effects.log: The corridor is cold glass and warm laughter. A Demon Realm guard looks at the ceiling. The century of peace begins quietly, with a hug.

choices.text: Share a private pot of the Realm's dark tea

mem.note: drank the Realm's wine with me after the treaty

effects.log: The dark tea is bitter and strong. You raise it to the peace. {npc} says it tastes like the last century and the next.

events.text: The Realm's Sovereign sends {npc} a polite gift and a private message: a faction of the Realm wishes the treaty broken. {He} may be recalled, or worse. The gift is a map of the secret route home, on a scroll, in an old blood-red ink.
events.arc: An Envoy to the Demon Realm

choices.text: Help {him} plan the return

mem.note: planned my escape from the Realm with me

effects.log: You plan the return. It takes a month of secret letters and a very quiet midnight. {npc} gets home with the treaty intact.

choices.text: Tell {him} to stay and finish the work

mem.note: told me to stay and finish

effects.log: You tell {him} to stay. {npc} stays. The faction is dealt with by the Sovereign in a week. The treaty holds, and so does {he}.

events.text: {npc} has taken up a new craft: building a cloud-barge from scratch, from a keel of moon-cedar to a mast of thunder-wood. It will take a century. The grotto fills with sawdust and curses. {He} announces that it will be the finest barge the Isles have seen.

choices.text: Offer to help with the rigging

mem.note: learned rigging to help with my barge

effects.log: You offer, and are given a thousand knots to learn. By midyear you are tying them in your sleep.

choices.text: Pay for the best materials

mem.note: bought the finest wood for my barge

effects.log: You pay for the moon-cedar and thunder-wood from your own stones. The barge is lovelier for it, and {npc} suspects the source.

choices.text: Tell {him} a barge is a foolish project

mem.note: called my barge foolish

effects.log: "Foolish," says {npc}, and goes on sawing. The sawing is a little louder.

events.text: Halfway through the century the keel cracks, a hairline, invisible except to {npc}, who finds it by touch. {He} stares at it all evening, silent. Then: "I have to start over." The grotto is full of two decades of work, and {he} means every word.

choices.text: Help tear it down and begin again

mem.note: tore down my barge with me and started again

effects.log: You tear it down together, board by board. The act is more intimate than any wedding. The new keel goes in with a ceremony of sawdust.

choices.text: Suggest the crack might be mended

mem.note: found a way to mend the cracked keel

effects.log: You suggest mending. {npc} considers, tests, and finds it will hold. The barge flies a crooked, lovable line for the rest of its days.

events.text: The barge is launched on a clear morning, bare of paint, humming with unused lift. {npc} puts a hand on the rail and cannot speak. The grotto gathers round. {He} turns, and says, "Come aboard. First flight. I would like you at the tiller."

choices.text: Take the tiller and fly the barge out

mem.note: let you take the tiller of my barge

effects.log: You take the tiller. The barge lifts like a promise kept. {npc} stands at the bow with the wind in the shape of their grin.

choices.text: Give the tiller back to {him}, and stand at the rail

mem.note: let me fly my own barge first

effects.log: "It is yours," you say. {npc} takes it and flies, and does not say a word, and does not need to.

events.text: The barge flies crooked, as it always will, and the Isles love it. Sailors on the Sea of Clouds point and say it is {npc}'s. A shipwright from the Pavilion of Falling Stars offers a fortune for the design. {npc} looks at the offer, and at you, and at the mended keel.

choices.text: Say sell, and build another

mem.note: sold my first barge on your word

effects.log: "I could build a better one," says {npc}. You sell it. The second barge is better, and never loved.

choices.text: Say keep the barge, crooked and all

mem.note: kept the crooked barge with me

effects.log: You say keep it. {npc} turns the offer down with a laugh. The barge hangs in the mooring-sky like a joke only you two are in on.

events.text: {npc} has taught three apprentices in the house, informally, over the decades. Now {he} wants to open a school: twenty pupils, a curriculum, an annual examination. The household, {he} says, will be the first classroom. {He} is clearly asking for the use of your grotto.

choices.text: Offer the grotto as a classroom

mem.note: opened our grotto as my school

effects.log: The grotto becomes a school overnight. Desks in the hall, a bell at the door. The house smells of ink and young qi.

choices.text: Offer a separate building on the isle

mem.note: offered me a school of my own

effects.log: You offer a separate building. {npc} is delighted and a little disappointed: a school in the home would have been a wonder.

choices.text: Ask for a quiet household instead

mem.note: asked me to keep a quiet house

effects.log: You say the house needs quiet. {npc} sighs, and takes the school to the Pavilion of Quiet Tea, and the matter closes.

events.text: The first year ends with an examination, and one pupil, a gifted and impossible child of the Jade Lotus House, outshines the rest. The House sends a petition to move the child to a grander school. {npc} reads it twice and says, softly, "They are right. But I do not want to lose them."

choices.text: Advise letting the child go

mem.note: let my best pupil go on your advice

effects.log: You advise it. {npc} signs the release with a steady hand. The child goes, tearful, and writes home every season.

choices.text: Advise offering the child a place as a junior teacher

mem.note: kept my best pupil as a teacher

effects.log: The child stays, and the school gains an assistant of terrifying ability. The House is mollified.

events.text: A century in, the school has a hundred pupils and a waiting list. At its anniversary, {npc} is given a lacquered plaque and a speech. The pupils present a scroll signed by all of them. At the bottom, in small brush, is your name. {npc} looks at you, astonished.

choices.text: Accept the plaque with {him}

mem.note: shared my anniversary plaque with you

effects.log: You hold the plaque together. The school applauds. Somewhere in the hall a small voice says you should have been a teacher.

choices.text: Step back and let {him} take the applause

mem.note: let me take my school's applause

effects.log: You step back. {npc} stands in the light of a hundred lanterns, and for a while is simply a teacher.

events.text: The child-teacher grows into a master in their own right, and at the school's second century they announce a rival academy across the clouds. {npc} is stung, then proud, then furious, then quiet. The rival opens in a spring of blossom. Pupils from both schools mingle in the market.

choices.text: Send the rival academy a gift of books

mem.note: sent my rival a gift of books

effects.log: The gift arrives with a short note. The rival, moved, returns a better gift. The two schools become, over time, a pair of sisters.

choices.text: Hold a joint examination between the two schools

mem.note: held a joint examination with my old pupil

effects.log: The joint examination is the talk of the Isles. Both schools shine, both fall short, and both learn.

events.text: The Nine Clouds Palace has lost a Seventh Seat, and the Palace holds a contest of three trials to choose a successor. {npc} has been invited to enter. It is a dangerous honour: three trials, one winner, and a house that watches. {He} asks if you would be willing to be {his} second.
events.arc: A Seat at the Nine Clouds Palace

choices.text: Accept and train {him} for the trials

mem.note: trained me for the Seventh Seat

effects.log: You accept. The training is relentless, silly, and tender. By the first trial, {npc} knows the shape of your voice in every corridor.

choices.text: Decline: the Palace is not your world

mem.note: declined to be my second

effects.log: "I understand," says {npc}. They enter with another second, a stranger. They do well. The distance is a small, polite one.

choices.text: Accept but set a limit: no sacrifices

mem.note: set a limit on my second

effects.log: You set the limit. {npc} agrees, with a reluctance they hide poorly, and the training begins with a signed paper.

events.text: The first trial is a riddle, the second an endurance, and the third a duel with an Elder of the Palace. On the eve of the third, the Elder sends {npc} a quiet offer: yield the trial, and a lesser seat is yours, safe, with no risk. {npc} brings it to you, unread.
events.arc: A Seat at the Nine Clouds Palace

choices.text: Tell {him} to fight the duel

mem.note: told me to fight the Elder

effects.log: You say fight. {npc} nods, folds the offer, and burns it in the lamp. The duel is long, and bruising.

choices.text: Tell {him} to take the lesser seat

mem.note: told me to take the safe seat

effects.log: You say take it. {npc} is silent, and then accepts. The lesser seat is comfortable, honourable, and not what they dreamed.

events.text: The duel ends in a draw, and the Palace, embarrassed, awards the Seventh Seat to {npc} by the Elder's own gesture. At the investiture the Elder bows. {npc} bows back, and then turns and bows to you, deeper, in front of the whole of the Palace.
events.arc: A Seat at the Nine Clouds Palace

choices.text: Bow back, and take {his} hand

mem.note: bowed to you at the Nine Clouds investiture

effects.log: You bow, and take their hand. The Palace murmurs. {npc} seems taller by a hand-width and lighter by a century.

choices.text: Slip away quietly before the feast

mem.note: slipped away rather than take my credit

effects.log: You slip away. {npc} finds you later on a balcony. "You did not stay for the banquet," {he} says. "I did not need to," you say. "I was there."

events.text: The lesser seat is a quiet, secure post, and {npc} does well in it. But in the third year {he} stops talking about the Palace at supper. In the fifth, {he} stops talking about the old dream altogether. One night, you ask: do they regret it? {He} does not answer at once.
events.arc: A Seat at the Nine Clouds Palace

choices.text: Say it is not too late to try again

mem.note: told me it was not too late

effects.log: You say so, honestly. {npc} says it is: the Seat is filled. They are quiet, and then say, thoughtfully, that a dream can be passed on.

choices.text: Say you are sorry you gave that advice

mem.note: apologised for the safe-seat advice

effects.log: You say sorry. {npc} says it was probably wise. A year later, they say it was wise, with more conviction. The regret becomes a lesson.

events.text: Decades later, the cloud-road narrows at the same turn, and {npc} is on the other barge again, grey at the temples. Two pilots, grown old and wise, wave each other through without a word. {npc} leans over the rail: "Still stubborn?"
events.arc: The Narrow Turn of the Cloud-Road

choices.text: Say you have learned to give way, sometimes

mem.note: threw a hundredth blossom at the old turn

effects.log: "Sometimes," {npc} agrees, and throws a pressed blossom, the hundredth, onto your deck.

choices.text: Say you will race them to the isle, for old times

mem.note: raced me again for old times

effects.log: The race is a draw, and both pilots are laughing too hard to steer. The sky is wide enough.

events.text: A new clerk of the Lotus Ledger, years on, finds the old entry that put you beside {npc} at that first audience and asks, reverently, whether it was fate or the seating chart. {npc} looks at you. You look at {npc}. The clerk waits with the brush raised.
events.arc: A Seat Beside the Lotus Ledger

choices.text: Say it was the seating chart

mem.note: blamed the seating chart with me

effects.log: The clerk writes it down with great seriousness. {npc} laughs so hard the ink spills across the page.

choices.text: Say it was fate, and let the clerk believe it

mem.note: let the clerk believe in fate

effects.log: The clerk beams and records it in gold. Some stories are better for being a little polished.

events.text: Mu Haeng, the Red Thread Elder, grown frail, visits the grotto on a quiet evening to ask whether the match was worth the meddling. {npc} pours the tea. The Elder looks from one of you to the other, and for once does not unroll a scroll.

choices.text: Tell the Elder it was worth every scheme

mem.note: thanked the Elder for the meddling

effects.log: The Elder weeps and claims the steam is to blame. The scroll of matches is left behind, with a new red circle: their own name.

choices.text: Tell the Elder to find a match for themselves now

mem.note: sent the Elder a match of their own

effects.log: "Impertinent," says the Elder, delighted. The year after, there is a very small wedding in a grotto nearby.

events.text: A comet crosses above the Pavilion of Falling Stars, the first in three hundred years, and the old chart that {npc} read for you is brought down from the wall for the occasion. The Pavilion elders compare the two. They fit exactly, with a margin the width of a hair.

choices.text: Ask {npc} what the hair of difference means

mem.note: stood under the comet with me

effects.log: "Room to be wrong," {npc} says. "That is where we live." You stand under the comet, glad of the gap.

choices.text: Hang the chart again, beside a new one

mem.note: hung a new chart beside the old

effects.log: You hang the new chart beside the old. The Pavilion has a custom, now: every comet, a chart for the two of you.

events.text: Years later a child of the Cloud-Weaver House asks to see the crooked strip of sunrise from Loom Night. {npc} unwraps it from a drawer. The child holds it up to the light and says it is the ugliest and most beautiful cloth in the House. The elders are not sure whether to be offended.

choices.text: Let the child keep it for a week

mem.note: lent our crooked strip to the House

effects.log: The child brings it back washed and pressed. A hundred apprentices now come to see it and are told it is a lesson in imperfection.

choices.text: Weave another strip with the child, badly, together

mem.note: wove a crooked strip with a child of the House

effects.log: The three of you weave a crooked strip by the lamp. It is a bad strip, and it is the best of the three.

events.text: No witness but the incense, and the Sea of Clouds going gold beneath the terrace. {npc} kneels across from you and says the old words that Dao partners have said above the clouds since the first Court: one road, two walking it, and whoever reaches the next stair waits. Then {he} adds, in {his} own voice: "And no going on alone. Promise."

choices.text: Promise it

effects.log: You promise. The incense burns to the end in one unbroken line of ash, which the Rolls count as a good omen.

choices.text: Promise to wait, not to never leave

effects.log: "I will wait," you say. "I cannot promise more than I know." {npc} thinks about it, and accepts the smaller true thing.

events.text: You swear the Dao vow with {npc} before the household's lanterns, and by the time the incense is out the whole house knows. Supper is very quiet. A kin of the house sets the dishes down a little too hard. {npc} reaches for your hand under the table and squeezes it once.

choices.text: Say something to the table

effects.log: You say that a vow on the road takes nothing from the house. Nobody answers. But somebody passes the rice.

choices.text: Let the silence be

effects.log: You eat in silence. Tomorrow will be easier, or it will not; tonight is for the vow.

events.text: You have come a long way to this terrace, {npc} to {his} realm and you to yours, two immortals the Floating Isles already talk about. A vow between such people is not a sweet thing. It is a contract with heaven's law. Above you, past the highest cloud, is the road you have just sworn to walk together.

choices.text: Look up at the clouds

effects.log: You both look up. It is very far. For the first time it does not seem too far.

choices.text: Look at {npc}

effects.log: You look at {npc} instead. {He} is already looking at you. The clouds can wait.

mem.note: was looked at instead of the sky

events.text: You come out of the breakthrough with the world sharper than before, and the first thing you feel is not your own power but {npc}'s: down the thread of the vow, {his} qi stirring in answer, like a second bell struck by the first, from across the whole Isle.

choices.text: Go to {him} at once

effects.log: You find {npc} on the terrace with {his} eyes closed, breathing the way you breathed an hour ago. You sit beside {him} and keep watch.

choices.text: Rest first

effects.log: You sleep a day and a night. When you wake, {npc} has left a cup of cloud-tea and a note: Felt it. Well done.

events.text: You break through, and a heartbeat later something in {npc} gives way too, a step behind you on the same white stair. The two of you look at each other across the room with the same astonished face. The scrolls say a vow is a thread. They did not say it would pull.

choices.text: Laugh

effects.log: You both laugh, at nothing, at everything. The spirit-servants think you have both deviated. Perhaps you have.

choices.text: Write it down

effects.log: You write down exactly what you felt, for the next pair who swear this vow and need to know.

events.text: {npc} breaks through in the night, and you wake before {he} does, sitting straight up in the dark with your heart pounding and your meridians full of someone else's light. It fades by morning. But you know a little more of the next stair than you did yesterday.

choices.text: Tell {him} what you felt

effects.log: {npc} listens with {his} chin in {his} hand. "So that is what it looks like from outside," {he} says.

choices.text: Keep it as a gift

effects.log: You keep it to yourself. Some things are better as a secret you share without saying.

events.text: {npc} comes out of seclusion a realm above where {he} went in, and stands in the doorway blinking at the cloud-light like someone who has slept a hundred years. Then {he} looks at you and says, slightly embarrassed: "I think I left a door open behind me. Come and see."

choices.text: Go and see

effects.log: You sit where {npc} sat. Something of the path is still in the air there, like warmth in a chair.

choices.text: Make {him} rest first

effects.log: You make {npc} eat and sleep. The door stays open a little longer than it would have. That seems right.

events.text: The first form of your paired art is nothing at all: you stand back to back with {npc} on a cloud-terrace and learn to breathe at the same time. It takes thirty years, which up here is a long spring. On the last day, a crane lands on your shoulder, then on {npc}'s, as if it cannot tell which is which.

choices.text: Keep breathing

effects.log: You keep breathing together long after the crane has gone. Neither of you wants to be the first to stop.

choices.text: Name the technique

effects.log: You call it the Crane's Mistake. {npc} groans. The name sticks anyway.

events.text: Halfway through the paired art you stop being able to tell whose blade is whose. {npc} parries a strike aimed at you before you see it; you finish a cut {he} began. The Jade Void Sect's sparring-masters refuse, after the third bout, to face the two of you together.

choices.text: Take it to the Court exhibition

effects.log: You show the art at a Court exhibition and win it so quickly the judges ask you to do it again, slower.

choices.text: Keep it between you

effects.log: You never show it in public. An art that only two know is an art nobody can answer.

events.text: The paired art is finished. You know it the way one knows a song is finished: there is nothing left to add. You and {npc} do it once more above the Sea of Clouds, one circle of light between two blades, and the clouds under you ring like a bell for a whole minute afterwards.

choices.text: Give it to a disciple one day

effects.log: You agree to teach it, one day, to a pair who deserve it. {npc} writes it down in two halves, one for each of you.

choices.text: Let it die with you

effects.log: You agree it is yours and {npc}'s alone, and will go where you go. That makes it heavier and more precious.

events.text: The Star Sea Pavilion sends an invitation: they have heard of a paired art that moves like one body, and would like to see two immortals bring it to the stage of the Starlit Court. {npc} turns the letter over twice. "It would mean showing them everything," {he} says.

choices.text: Accept and show it

effects.log: You accept. The Pavilion watches with its mouth open, and the art leaves your hands the moment it is seen.

choices.text: Refuse and keep it quiet

effects.log: You refuse, politely. The Pavilion is offended in the way of a house that wanted to be impressed.

events.text: {npc} and you teach the first line of the paired art to a young pair of the Jade Lotus House who ask nicely. It goes badly. They cannot breathe together; they laugh, they quarrel, they blame each other. After a month one of them says to the other, "I think we are doing it."

choices.text: Teach the second line too

effects.log: You teach the second line. Somewhere in the corridor, {npc} lets out a breath that has been held for fifty years.

choices.text: Stop there, it is enough

effects.log: You stop. A line learnt slowly is a line learnt well. The young pair bow, awkwardly, and walk away arguing.

events.text: You and {npc} try the paired art in the dark for the first time, with the lamps out, to learn it by feel alone. It is a quiet, odd, intimate hour. At the end you find you are standing hand in hand and neither of you remembers deciding to.

choices.text: Stay in the dark a moment longer

effects.log: You stay. The clouds beneath the terrace move without sound. When the lamps are lit again, neither of you mentions it.

choices.text: Light the lamp and go on

effects.log: You light the lamp and drill the next form until midnight. It comes cleaner for the hour in the dark.

events.text: A season in the Inner Grotto with {npc}, the door sealed, one lamp between you. You do not speak for weeks. You do not need to. By the end you can feel the turn of {his} qi the way one feels the turn of a tide, and you come out into the cloud-light with your eyes watering and your heart very quiet.

choices.text: Go straight back to training

effects.log: You train that same afternoon. Everything is a little easier, the way a road is easier the second time.

choices.text: Sit in the sun together

effects.log: You sit on the terrace step in the sun for a whole day, saying nothing. It is the best day of the year.

events.text: In the third month of the seclusion {npc} speaks, very softly: a question about the Dao that you have circled for a thousand years without daring to ask. Hearing it in someone else's voice, you suddenly know the answer. Then you are not sure. Then you know it again.

choices.text: Answer {him}

effects.log: You answer. {npc} is quiet so long you think {he} has fallen asleep. Then: "Yes," {he} says. "That."

choices.text: Let the question stand

effects.log: You do not answer. Some questions are better as company than as answers.

events.text: A seclusion in the Cloud Grotto is a strange thing: no dark, no door, only a bank of cloud that closes over you both like water and opens again a season later. {npc} comes out of it smiling at something {he} will not tell you, and you find you do not need to be told.

choices.text: Trust the smile

effects.log: You trust it. Up here, on this road, that is a kind of cultivation too.

choices.text: Ask anyway

effects.log: "Later," {npc} says, "when you catch up." You laugh and chase {him} across the clouds.

events.text: Your qi slips its bank in the Inner Grotto, a flood with no floor, and not one meridian still obeys you. Then {npc}'s voice finds you down the vow-thread, counting the old breathing numbers aloud. Each number is a stone to set a foot on, and you cross.

choices.text: Thank {him} with your life

effects.log: "You would have done the same," {npc} says, then, being honest: "I hope you would."

choices.text: Ask why {he} risked the crossing

effects.log: A flood like that takes the rescuer along. "I know," {npc} says, and pours the tea.

events.text: The deviation is {npc}'s this time: in the lamp light you see {his} face go grey and {his} hands begin to shake. Every instinct says to run for a healer of the Ministries, to break the seclusion. You put your hand on {his} back instead.

choices.text: Hold steady

effects.log: You hold steady through the night. In the morning {npc} opens {his} eyes and says your name, and you start breathing again.

choices.text: Break the seal and run for help

effects.log: You break the seal. The healer comes; {npc} lives. Later {he} asks, quietly, why you did not trust the vow.

events.text: Deep in the seclusion, {npc}'s heart demon rises in the form of a hall of mirrors, each one showing a different end to your road together. {He} cannot move. The mirrors show you leaving, dying, rising alone. You can hear them whispering. You can only reach {him} through the thread.

choices.text: Speak through the thread, steadily

effects.log: You speak through the thread of the vow, plain words, all night. In the morning the mirrors are gone.

choices.text: Reach with qi and break the nearest mirror

effects.log: You break a mirror with your qi, and feel the crack in your own chest. {npc} survives, and so, barely, do you.

events.text: A rumour comes to the house, the kind with a sharp end: {npc} was seen at the Jade Court with a stranger, at night, at a door with no sign. By the time {npc} comes home, three people have told you three versions. {He} sees your face and stops in the doorway.

choices.text: Ask {him} plainly

effects.log: "A physician," {npc} says. "For a cough I did not want you to worry about." It is true. You are both ashamed, differently.

choices.text: Say nothing and watch

effects.log: You say nothing. {npc} knows something is wrong and cannot find out what. A week of cold dinners follows.

events.text: {npc} has found a manual: half a technique of the old immortals, the kind that could carry one of you a stair ahead and leave the other standing. There is only one copy. {He} sets it on the table between you and folds {his} hands, waiting to see what you will do.

choices.text: Push it to {him}

effects.log: You push it across. {npc} looks at it a long time, then tears it carefully in two and hands you half. "We learn it together, or not at all."

choices.text: Take it

effects.log: You take it. {npc} says nothing. You learn it alone, and it is a good technique, and it tastes of ash.

events.text: On a stair above a gorge of cloud, the stone gives way under {npc}. {He} catches the edge with one hand. You could reach {him}. You could also fall. There is perhaps a breath to decide in, and {npc} is looking at you, not at the drop.

choices.text: Reach

effects.log: You reach. For one long moment you are both hanging over the gorge. Then you are both on the stair, soaked, laughing like fools.

choices.text: Tell {him} to climb

effects.log: "Climb!" you shout, and {npc} climbs, by {his} own strength, and does not look at you on the walk home.

events.text: A rival of the Demon Realm offers {npc} a hoard of spirit stones to tell them where you meditate at dawn. {npc} tells you about the offer at supper, between two mouthfuls of soup, as if mentioning the weather. Then {he} asks, lightly: "Did you ever wonder if I would take it?"

choices.text: Tell the truth: no, never

effects.log: "Never," you say. {npc} smiles into {his} soup. That was the right answer, and it was also true.

choices.text: Tell the truth: once

effects.log: "Once," you admit. {npc} puts {his} spoon down. "Thank you for telling me," {he} says, and means it, and is hurt.

events.text: {npc} finds you alone on the corridor of the grotto and does not move out of the way. "You swore a road with one of us," {he} says, "and the rest of us are only the household now. I want to know what that makes me." {His} voice is very calm. {His} hands are not.

choices.text: Tell {him} what {he} is to you

effects.log: You tell {npc}, in plain words, what {he} is to you, which is not the road but is not less. {He} listens to every word.

choices.text: Say the vow is not for discussion

effects.log: "The vow is the vow," you say. {npc} steps aside. The grotto is very cold for a decade.

events.text: {npc} has started training at dawn, hard, alone, on the far terrace, where you cannot help seeing. It takes you a season to understand. {He} is not trying to be stronger. {He} is trying to be chosen. When you come onto the terrace, {npc} stops and waits, sword lowered.

choices.text: Spar with {him}

effects.log: You spar until the sun is high. You say nothing about vows. Afterwards {npc} laughs for the first time in a decade.

choices.text: Tell {him} to stop

effects.log: "You are hurting yourself," you say. "Yes," says {npc}. "I noticed that too." {He} does not stop.

events.text: You have gone two stairs past {npc} now, and it shows in everything: {he} cannot follow your sparring, cannot feel the qi you speak of, sits in on your seclusions like a guest at someone else's prayer. One night {he} says it first. "You can go on without me. I will not hold it against you."

choices.text: Say you will wait

effects.log: "I swore to wait," you say. "I will." {npc} cries, then, for the first time in your marriage, quietly, into your shoulder.

choices.text: Say nothing yet

effects.log: You do not answer that night. Both of you lie awake listening to the other not sleep.

events.text: You rise another stair, and {npc} cannot follow the weather up there. At the Court the clerks greet you first and {npc} second. One of them says to {npc}, kindly, that it is a great thing to be married to someone who goes far. {npc} smiles, and the smile does not reach anywhere.

choices.text: Take {him} aside and say it is not true

effects.log: "I do not go far without you," you say. {npc} does not believe it yet, but holds the sentence like a stone in a pocket.

choices.text: Train {him} for a season

effects.log: You spend a season hauling {npc} up to the next stair, step by step. It is not enough, but it is something.

events.text: {npc} is two stairs ahead of you now. {He} slows when you walk together, shortens {his} stride, pretends not to feel the weather that only {his} realm can feel. You see the effort. It is kinder than anything {he} could say, and it is unbearable.

choices.text: Ask {him} to stop pretending

effects.log: "Go at your own pace," you say. "I will catch up." {npc} looks at you a long time and lengthens {his} stride, a little.

choices.text: Train harder in secret

effects.log: You train at night, alone, until your hands are raw. {npc} finds the bandages and says nothing about them.

events.text: A Jade Court herald comes for {npc}: a summons to the upper terraces, the first of a series. You are not named. {He} reads it twice and hands it to you, wordless. "I will not go if you ask me not to," {he} says. It is the kind of offer that is a trap in both directions.

choices.text: Tell {him} to go

effects.log: "Go," you say. "I will follow." {npc} goes, and writes every season, and the letters are the best thing about the decade.

choices.text: Ask {him} to wait a year

effects.log: You ask for a year. {npc} gives it, and is gentle about it, and the year is a long one for both.

events.text: One morning you stand beside {npc} at the edge of the cloud-terrace and feel the same weather {he} feels, the same faint pull of the next stair. Neither of you is ahead. Neither of you says anything about it. {npc} just hands you your sword, the way {he} used to, before.

choices.text: Train together like before

effects.log: You train together until noon, and it is exactly like before, and better.

choices.text: Thank {him} for waiting

effects.log: "I did not wait," {npc} says. "I walked slowly. That is different." You decide it is not, and say so.

events.text: You reach the stair where {npc} has been standing for fifty years, and find {him} sitting on the top step with a pot of tea and two cups. The second cup is already poured. "I guessed the day," {he} says. "I was off by a year. I kept pouring."

choices.text: Sit and drink the cold tea

effects.log: The tea is stone cold and the best you have ever tasted. You sit through the afternoon on the same step, finally level.

choices.text: Pour a fresh cup for both

effects.log: You pour fresh tea. {npc} laughs, and the old cup is poured out over the edge of the cloud, a small libation to the long wait.

events.text: {npc} sets down the cup you shared the vow from, cold tea still in it, and tips it empty over the terrace rail. The road vow is spent, {he} says, gently, like a debt paid. The house, the roof and the name remain. Out on the clouds a crane calls twice, unanswered.

choices.text: Say the debt was an honour

effects.log: You say it, and mean it. {npc} nods slowly, the way one nods to a ledger that finally balances.

mem.note: called our road a debt paid

choices.text: Take the empty cup to keep

effects.log: You take the cup. It will hold nothing for a long time, and you find it is good company.

mem.note: took the empty cup

events.text: {npc} comes to the Cloud Terrace at dawn, with the vow-scroll in one hand, and burns it in the brazier without a word. You watch it curl. There is no anger in it; it is the tidiest thing {he} has ever done. "The road was ours," {he} says. "The house is still ours."

choices.text: Say the house is enough

effects.log: You say it. It is not enough, and {npc} knows, and it is very kind of both of you to say it anyway.

choices.text: Ask {him} to keep one line of the scroll

effects.log: You ask for a line. {npc} tears it off the edge before the flame reaches it and puts it in your palm.

mem.note: saved one line of our vow from the fire

events.text: {dcp_name} is gone. The vow does not say what to do now; the old scrolls are silent on it, as if nobody who swore it ever lived long enough to ask. You find the half of the incense stick in a drawer, still with the ash on it, and you sit holding it until the cloud-light goes.

choices.text: Walk the road alone, for both

effects.log: You will walk it for both of you, then. Every step from now on counts double, or it does not count at all.

choices.text: Burn the incense for {dcp_name}

effects.log: You burn it on the terrace. The vow goes where {dcp_name} went. You will have to find your own reasons now.

events.text: An immortal's grief is a slow thing: a century of waking up and reaching for a thread that is not there. The household is kind and careful, and does not mention {dcp_name}'s name at table. On the hundredth day a servant leaves a cup of {dcp_name}'s favourite tea at your door, unasked.

choices.text: Drink it, and say the name aloud

effects.log: You drink it, and say the name aloud for the first time in a hundred days. The household breathes out, and so do you.

choices.text: Put the cup in the shrine

effects.log: You set the cup in the shrine, still warm. It will go cold, and be refilled, and you will keep the practice for a thousand years.

events.text: Up here, a year is nothing; a decade is a long afternoon. Below, {dcp_name} is still climbing. You keep a seat for them at the edge of the jade terrace, and every so often you part the clouds and look down, though you know you will not find them, and come back and sit.

choices.text: Keep the seat

effects.log: You keep it. The other immortals have learned not to sit in it. One of them leaves a cup of tea there, now and then.

choices.text: Send a dream below

effects.log: You send a dream down through the clouds: a stair, a terrace, a seat. Whether it arrives, you cannot know.

events.text: An immortal of the Jade Court asks you, kindly, why you never take a new companion up here, where there are so many who would. You try to explain about {dcp_name}, and a vow, and the white stairs, and find you have been talking for an hour. The immortal has stopped asking and started listening.

choices.text: Finish the story

effects.log: You finish it. The immortal bows to you, deeply, and goes away, and does not ask again.

choices.text: Stop and laugh at yourself

effects.log: You stop and laugh. "It is a long road," you say. "I am only halfway through telling it."

events.text: A crane comes up through the clouds with a scrap of news: {dcp_name} has crossed the thousandth step on the White Stairs. It has been a hundred years since the last word. You read the scrap three times, then walk the length of the terrace, then read it again.

choices.text: Send the crane back with a cup of tea

effects.log: The crane takes the little cup in its beak with an air of grave responsibility. The tea will be cold by the time it arrives. It is the thought.

choices.text: Climb down to meet them at the halfway landing

effects.log: You descend to the halfway landing and wait there, on the cold stone, like a pilgrim. You arrive three days early.

events.text: {npc} is at the top of the white stairs, exactly where the vow said {he} would be. {He} has kept a seat for you at the edge of the cloud terrace, and the cup on it is still warm, as if {he} had known the hour. "You were long," {npc} says. "I did say not to be long."

choices.text: Sit down

effects.log: You sit. The clouds go gold beneath you. Neither of you says anything for a very long time, and nothing needs to be said.

choices.text: Say you are here now

effects.log: "I am here now," you say. "Then we can begin," says {npc}, "the next part of the road."

events.text: You waited above the clouds so long that waiting became a kind of cultivation, and now {npc} comes up the white stairs, out of breath, older and somehow younger, and stops two steps below you as if not quite sure you are real. You hold out your hand, the way you did once on a ledge above a gorge.

choices.text: Pull {him} up the last steps

effects.log: You pull {npc} up the last two steps. "You kept the seat," {he} says. "I kept the seat," you agree.

choices.text: Let {him} climb them alone

effects.log: You let {npc} climb the last two by {his} own strength, because that was the vow too. {He} reaches the top laughing.
